title: Shared-Prefix KV Reuse Across Standard LoRA Adapters: Quality and Serving Tradeoffs
summary: The technique replaces per-specialist re-prefilling of a shared context by computing the backbone's prefix KV cache once and reusing it across already-trained standard LoRA adapters. The cost is a small, inconsistent quality degradation on held-out tasks (e.g., -4.6 to -0.8 EM on GSM8K depending on token budget and seed), and the tested implementation copied rather than physically shared KV storage, yielding only 12% lower two-branch peak memory. It can fail when adapter quality degrades beyond tolerance, since no boundary-selection rule or quality equivalence is established and partial recomputation showed no demonstrated benefit.
rationale: The approach is deployable on constrained single-GPU infrastructure and offers real TTFT savings at long contexts, but the inconsistent quality deltas and absent memory savings mean it must be validated on the reader's specific adapters and workload before production use.
